findings.title: The loaded pack set comes from each process's environment, but every process shares one store
findings.claim: The pack set, which decides which kinds, lenses, decisions and prompts exist, is resolved per process. PLANROOM_PACKS adds to it and is read from each process's environment. Every process folds and scans the same store, and a repo's active snapshot is whichever scan event came last. So two processes with different environments see different models, and the last scanner silently decides everyone's actual layer. There is also no actor rule on PLANROOM_PACKS: any agent's Bash can set it and load a pack that carries policy. The stated reason for dealing no card ("a person listed it") does not hold for an environment variable.
findings.evidence: Verified by reading the docs; there is no code yet. architecture.md:539 says packs load from built-ins, then config.toml, then PLANROOM_PACKS, and that "a person chose it by listing it in config or PLANROOM_PACKS, so loading it deals no card" (DR-60, decisions.md:1157). architecture.md:363: "the active snapshot at `at` is the one named by its last `scan` event". architecture.md:243: freshness compares HEAD with the active snapshot, and packs_hash is not mentioned. snapshots are UNIQUE on (repo, commit_id, purpose, packs_hash) (architecture.md:461). watch and serve are long-lived and keep an in-memory fold (architecture.md:155-156, 372). The fold drops unknown kinds with a warning (architecture.md:364). The mod's tool.check guard covers PLANROOM_PERSON_KEY, store files and person-only commands, but not PLANROOM_PACKS (architecture.md:399-403). feature_list.json S10 ci_path.steps puts PLANROOM_PACKS only on the scan line (`PLANROOM_PACKS=... planroom scan --json`). The next steps, `planroom ask kinds`, `map --lens flags` and `decide`, run without it. KICKOFF R10 (several sessions, one workspace, every surface consistent), R5 ("nothing the AI invents counts until a person accepts it") and the S10 assertions.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) S10 as written fails. Following shell semantics, `ask kinds` and `map --lens flags` run in processes with no toy pack, so flags.flag is not listed, the lens is unknown, and the fold drops the flags facts. (b) A person's mod session started its detached `serve` and `watch` without PLANROOM_PACKS. An agent then rescans with it, or the other way round. The active snapshot flips between pack sets on every scan. Person overrides on nodes from the toy pack become orphaned and raise rescan.retarget person cards, which come back when the other process scans again. (c) A prompt-injected agent runs `PLANROOM_PACKS=/tmp/x planroom scan`. Its pack declares a low-stakes decision with effect set_prop on code.service `role`, or an `infer` prompt. Prefills and infer outputs apply as inferred facts, not ghosts (architecture.md:333-335). Shared answers such as `unmonitored` change for every surface, with no card and no person involved.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the pack set workspace state. Packs come from the trusted `.planroom/config.toml` only. The store's meta records the resolved pack list and the packs_hash of the last scan, and a process whose resolved set differs refuses writes with `packs_mismatch`, or folds with the recorded set. Adding or removing an out-of-tree pack becomes a person-only path, for example `scan --pack DIR` confirmed on /dev/tty or with a mod press, which writes the config. Drop PLANROOM_PACKS, or limit it to `doctor --pack`. Rewrite the S10 ci_path to add the packs through that path from a directory outside the tree. Add a test in which two processes with different environments scan alternately and the active snapshot never flips.

findings.title: The DecisionKind contract can't express several of v0.1's own decision kinds
findings.claim: DecisionKind has a node-or-edge `subject` kind, a `when` that is a field/value predicate, choice `options` that are a static map, and a closed set of five effects. Five of the eleven v0.1 kinds need something outside that. So R9's "every decision kind has a declared policy" can't be met as pack data, and a new kind of the same shape, such as "choose among candidate nodes", can't be added without engine special-casing.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:615 `subject: String // a node or edge kind`; :616 `when: Predicate // { field = value } or { field = { lt | gt | in = ... } }`; :630 `Choice { instructions, options: IndexMap<String, String>, auto_choices }`; :620 and architecture.md:817 give the effect set as none, lint, set_prop, put_edge or retract_edge. Against that: `machines_same` has the subject "machine pair in the 0.5 to 0.8 band" (architecture.md:840), which is not a node or edge, and nothing computes the Jaccard band. `override_retarget` has the subject "orphaned override", a vanished target, and its effect is to retarget an edit, which none of the five effects does (architecture.md:823, 841). `file_component` and `attach_target` are choices among per-subject candidate nodes (architecture.md:836, 842), so they can't be static options, and `auto_choices` can't name them. `file_component`'s precheck "files no path rule placed" uses a term defined nowhere. `commit_addresses_thread`'s precheck, "a later commit on the PR branch touches the thread's file within 10 lines of its anchor" (architecture.md:788), is not a field predicate. EvalCase.label is "an option" (contracts.md:655), with no per-case options. KICKOFF R9; S7 (tier A) runs `file_component` as an auto candidate with 40 tune and 60 holdout cases.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer writing packs/code/pack.toml can't declare `file_component` or `override_retarget`, and can't write their eval cases, so the loader rejects them as pack_invalid. The only way out is hard-coding them in `app` by name. Then the S7 eval table can't report `file_component` as designed, its auto policy is undefined because `auto_choices` can't list dynamic candidates, and a pack author who copies the pattern for a "which owner?" kind finds the contract can't express it, which breaks S10's promise for decision kinds beyond the trivial boolean.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the contract once, generically. (1) `options_from = { shape, params, max }` gives a choice its candidates from a query over the subject, sent as per-request Jev criteria and stored in each EvalCase as `options`, with `auto_choices` replaced by `auto_when_choice_in` a predicate or dropped for dynamic kinds. (2) A subject can be a role subject, a typed `Target::Role { role, key }` that the role raiser supplies. (3) `when` may reference props that built-in extractors precompute: `review_threads` sets `props.touched_after_anchor`, `files` sets `props.placed_by_rule`, and a machines built-in linker emits `machines.describes` candidate edges with the Jaccard score as confidence, so `machines_same` has subject `machines.describes` and `when = { confidence = { lt = 0.8, gt = 0.5 } }`. (4) Add a `retarget` effect, or make retargeting the role's built-in effect. Add a packs.rs test that every v0.1 kind validates against the contract.

findings.title: Several v0.1 questions are not pipelines of the fixed shapes, and S6 drift has no designed home
findings.claim: The design says a question is pack data, a pipeline of one to three shapes from a closed set of twelve. Four of the questions the v0.1 packs list can't be built that way: `drift`, `kinds`, `stage` and `lint`. Machine pairing, which S6 drift depends on, is assigned to no shape, linker, built-in or role. Five of the twelve shapes are used by only one pack each, so the claimed bar for a kernel shape (two packs) already fails. In practice the pattern is one kernel shape per domain, which undercuts "new domains need no core change" for any domain beyond S10's trivial one.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:572-574: `QuestionDecl { steps: Vec<ShapeStep> /* 1 to 3 */ }` and `enum Shape { Node, Find, Neighbors, Path, Why, Filter, Compare, Order, Subgraph, Tree, Machine, Checks }`. architecture.md:722 and DR-15: "A new question is pack data. A new shape is a kernel change, so the bar for one is that two packs need it." The machines pack lists the question `drift` (architecture.md:733), run as `planroom ask drift` (architecture.md:1005; feature_list.json S6 steps at lines 312 and 318), but drift is `diff(machine A, machine B)` after Jaccard pairing (architecture.md:735), and no shape diffs or pairs. The code pack's `kinds` (architecture.md:728) lists pack metadata, not the graph; S10 asserts it (feature_list.json:542). The plan pack's `stage` returns "the stage's method checklist, the attached slice and the lint state" (architecture.md:976), and its `lint` is not a shape. The "Used by" column (architecture.md:694-707) puts compare and order on release only, subgraph on observability only, tree on artifacts only, and machine and checks on machines only. Breakdown.touched (contracts.md:511) has the domain-generic `tree` shape computing "the touched components" of a PR without saying how. KICKOFF R11 and S6 (tier B).
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer can't write the machines pack's `drift`, or the code pack's `kinds`, as a QuestionDecl, because the closed Shape enum and the generated input schema reject them. They special-case the question IDs in `crates/planroom/src/app`, which no boundary check covers. S6 drift then depends on code that isn't designed, and machine pairing (thresholds 0.8 and 0.5, the `machines_same` hand-off) lands in whatever crate is handy. A later domain that needs a comparison question repeats the pattern, and the claim that a new question is pack data stops being true.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the four questions a designed home. Add a `diff` shape (two node sets or slice refs into kernel::diff, restricted by edge kinds), which machines drift and any future layer or version comparison can share. Produce pairing as data: a machines built-in linker emits `machines.describes` edges with the overlap as confidence, and the question becomes `filter describes`, then `diff`. Make `kinds`, `stage` and `lint` catalogue reads, not pack questions (`schema --kinds`, `intent lint`, `intent next --stage S --dry`), or add a `meta` shape. Either keep the two-pack bar and record each single-pack shape's exception in DR-15, or restate the bar honestly. Add a packs.rs test that every built-in pack's questions parse into shape pipelines with no app special cases.

findings.title: Container IDs depend on which pack classifies the container, so a pack change re-IDs nodes and orphans corrections
findings.claim: A Container-level node's ID prefix comes from its kind's pack, and two packs may not share a prefix. Compose classifies services through `[[image_roles]]` merged across packs, and the observability pack maps the collector, Prometheus and Grafana to its own `observability.infra`. So a service's ID changes whenever the set of loaded packs, or a built-in pack's image globs, change: on a pack load or unload, or on an engine upgrade that adds a glob. Every person override on that container then targets a vanished ID. DR-46 rejected one prefix per kind precisely so that "a reclassified container keeps its ID", but the fix works only within one pack.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:304: "Several kinds of one pack may share a prefix, such as `container`... so a reclassified container keeps its ID. Two packs declaring one prefix is `pack_invalid`." architecture.md:670 and DR-46: the observability pack's `[[image_roles]]` map images to `observability.infra`, and compose reads the merged table. contracts.md:550: `id_prefix /* owned by one pack */`. architecture.md:367: a vanished target raises `rescan.retarget`, which `override_retarget` binds as a person-stakes card (architecture.md:841). KICKOFF R6: "Corrections survive every rescan. A scan never silently overrides a person's edit."
findings.failure_scenario: A person regroups `prometheus` (then `ws:infra:prometheus`) under a `monitoring` group. A later release adds `victoriametrics*` to the observability pack's image_roles, or an out-of-tree pack adds a more specific glob for an image the code pack treated as `code.service`. On the next scan the container gets a new ID under another prefix, the regroup stops applying, and the person gets a retarget card for an edit they never touched. The same happens to every override and intended rule on that container, including boundary rules, which then stop being checked by reconciliation.
findings.proposed_fix: Key structural IDs by level and source, not by the classifying pack. Let the kernel reserve a level prefix (`container`, `component`), which any pack's kind at that level may use. Or derive a compose service's ID from `ws:container:<service>` whatever its kind, and let the kind and role change underneath. Add a test that loading and unloading a pack that only adds an image role keeps every container ID and every override applied.

findings.title: The domain-free check misses the coupling the design creates, and flags harmless generic words
findings.claim: The kernel's literal scan matches only built-in kind and relation names, bare or prefixed. The plan lint the kernel must run uses plan semantics: MECE sibling overlap, a Must below the MVP line, and a ladder under 2 rungs. None of these fits the four RuleTypes, so the kernel will hard-code prop names and item types (`moscow`, `mvp_line`, `done_test`, `next_action`), which the scan can't see. Meanwhile bare names such as `file`, `state`, `step`, `commit`, `tag`, `job`, `image`, `section`, `module`, `package` and `person` are ordinary words in kernel code. Adding a built-in pack kind with a common name can then fail the kernel build, forcing a kernel edit when a domain is added.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md:132 and :156; DR-45: "The domain-free scan fails on a kernel string literal that equals a built-in pack kind or relation name, with or without its `<pack>.` prefix." contracts.md:575 lists RuleType as `RequiresProp | RequiresEdge | MinChildren | Covers`. architecture.md:970-972 lists the lint "sibling overlap (MECE)", "no MVP line; a Must below the line" and "a ladder under 2 rungs". traceability.md:30 cites the test `kernel/tests/lint.rs::mece_overlap`. The bare kind names are in architecture.md:728-733. KICKOFF R16: "Boundaries are enforced by tooling, not convention. The kernel depends on no domain."
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds a `mece_overlap` rule in the kernel that reads `props.scope_tags` and `props.moscow == "must"`, and the check passes. Later, adding a built-in `k8s` pack with kind `k8s.node` or `k8s.job` fails `cargo xtask check boundaries` on an unrelated kernel literal, such as a "node" serde key or a "job" in a summary string, so adding a domain needs a kernel edit.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the missing generic rule types with their parameters (`Disjoint { field }`, `Ordered { field, before, rank_prop }`, `MinLen { field }`) so the plan pack declares MECE, the MVP line and the ladder as data. Extend the scan to the prop names and item types the built-in packs declare. Match only `<pack>.<name>` and the names that are distinctive to a pack, with an explicit allow-list for generic words recorded in boundaries.toml.

findings.title: The pack schema has one-off tables and closed sets, and merge conflicts are unspecified
findings.claim: Several top-level PackFile tables each serve one built-in or one pack: `[[languages]]` for `files`, `[[image_roles]]` for compose, and `[[stages]]`, which is plan pack only. So the next built-in that needs cross-pack configuration, such as k8s workload kinds or Terraform resource types, changes the contract. Closed enums contradict the "one more built-in, no kernel change" claims: Tier has no Precise variant, although fact merging ranks "precise" first, and `Query.language` is a closed enum while `[[languages]]` is open data. How merged tables resolve conflicts is undefined: two packs claiming `.rb`, overlapping image globs, or two lenses with `default = true`. `[[hints]]` lets an out-of-tree pack declare new hint kinds, but only built-in linkers can consume them.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:532-545 (`languages`, `image_roles`, `stages // plan pack only`). contracts.md:380: `enum Tier { Universal, Syntactic, Config, Pattern, Inference, Linked }`, against architecture.md:319 ("precise, then syntactic, then config, then pattern, then universal") and architecture.md:612 ("one more built-in reading an existing `index.scip`; no kernel change"). contracts.md:559 (`language: Language`) and :568 (`LinkerDecl { builtin, options }` only). architecture.md:539 ("The `[[languages]]` and `[[image_roles]]` tables merge across loaded packs"), with no precedence rule. The extractor contract requires byte-identical output.
findings.failure_scenario: An out-of-tree `ruby-rails` pack and the Ruby pack both declare `rb`, with different comment markers. Which one wins depends on undocumented merge behaviour, and comment blanking, and so the facts, change with load order. The SCIP reader, the first tier-3 built-in, has no Tier to report and needs a contract change. A pack author declares a hint kind and finds nothing can join it.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the special tables with one generic `[[tables]] builtin = NAME, rows = [...]` that each built-in reads, merged in documented pack order, with duplicate keys as `pack_invalid` unless a row sets `override = true`. Add `Precise` to Tier now. Make two `default = true` lenses `pack_invalid` unless one of them is the code pack's. Document that hint kinds from out-of-tree packs need an existing built-in linker, or drop `[[hints]]` for out-of-tree packs.

findings.title: Out-of-tree packs can't build on any v0.1 domain except code
findings.claim: `requires` is limited to `[]` or `["code"]`, and every referenced kind must belong to the pack, `code` or the kernel. So an out-of-tree domain can't extend observability (an SLO or on-call pack over `observability.alert`), release, artifacts or machines. That is stricter than KICKOFF's "depend inward, never sideways": every built-in pack is inward of an out-of-tree pack. The self-test even treats `requires = ["observability"]` on the toy pack as a violation.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md:142-143 (`requires = [[], ["code"]]   # the only allowed values`) and :158 ("every referenced kind belongs to the pack, `code` or the kernel"); repo-layout.md:173, self-test step 6; DR-9's round-1 amendment ("a pack may require only a pack in a lower ring, which in v0.1 means `code` or nothing"). KICKOFF R16 ("Packs and adapters depend inward, never sideways") and R11.
findings.failure_scenario: A user writes an `slo` pack that adds `slo.objective` with parent `observability.alert` and a lens over `observability.watches`. The loader rejects it with pack_invalid, so this extension needs a core change: editing boundaries.toml and the loader rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Define rings by origin. Built-in packs form the inner rings, ordered as they are now. An out-of-tree pack may require any built-in pack but no other out-of-tree pack, which keeps the rule acyclic and inward. Change self-test step 6 to plant a built-in pack that requires an outer one, or an out-of-tree pack that requires another out-of-tree pack.

findings.title: The declarative runner quietly assumes the code pack's file nodes
findings.claim: Emit templates use a bare `$file` as an edge's `from` and as a hint's `scope`, but the documented reference grammar names only `@alias:`, an ID, `@id:KIND:KEY` and `@ext:`, and Hint.scope is a NodeId. Resolving a bare path therefore means the engine's runner knows that files are `code.file` nodes with the prefix `file`. That is an undocumented core dependency on one pack, and it means a pack with `requires = []` can't emit from files.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:564-569 (`from = "$file"`, and the reference forms for targets and parents); the Ruby pack at architecture.md:643 and :649 (`from = "$file"`, `scope = "$file"`); contracts.md:371 (`scope: NodeId`) and :564 (`to /* @alias:..., an ID, @id:KIND:KEY, or @ext:NAME */`, with `from` unspecified).
findings.failure_scenario: A pack author writes `from = "@id:code.file:$file"` according to the grammar, while the built-in packs write `$file`. The two forms resolve differently, or one fails. An independent pack with `requires = []` that emits `from = "$file"` validates but references a kind it doesn't require.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit kernel-owned reference form, `@file:$file`, which resolves to the node a universal-tier file fact defines, and require it in `from`, `to`, `parent` and `scope`. Or make the file node kernel vocabulary next to `kernel.external`. Validate that bare paths are rejected.

findings.title: Plan item types form a second kind system beside [[kinds]]
findings.claim: DR-45 moved plan items into `kernel.item` with a `type` prop. Item types and their prop schemas are declared in `[[stages]].items` (ItemType), which parallels KindDecl's props, and `[[stages]]` is plan pack only. So there are two typing mechanisms, two prop validators, and subjects and predicates like `subject = "kernel.item"` with `when = { "props.type" = ... }`, while no other pack can declare Intent-level items.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:577-580 (`StageDecl.items: Vec<ItemType>`, and `ItemType { id /* the kernel.item type */, props: Value }`) against KindDecl at :550-553; contracts.md:545 (`stages // plan pack only`); architecture.md:729 and :804; DR-45. KICKOFF R11 ("The core data model is simple") and the constraint "no speculative abstractions".
findings.failure_scenario: A release-planning pack wants a `release_train` intent item. It can't declare one without `[[stages]]`, which is plan pack only, and if it declares a normal kind at the Intent level, the reconciler and `attach.target`, which read `kernel.item`, ignore it.
findings.proposed_fix: Let ItemType be an ordinary `[[kinds]]` entry carrying `extends = "kernel.item"`. The kernel then treats any kind that extends `kernel.item` as a plan item, and validates props by kind, once. Allow `[[stages]]` in any pack, keyed by project template, or document why it stays single.

findings.title: Pack data carries no visual identity, and the canvas chooses views by lens ID
findings.claim: The design language gives each relationship kind its own yarn color and each container kind its own block color, but LensDecl and RelationDecl have no color or style field, and the block tokens are named after code and observability kinds. The canvas opens Anatomy and Machine views by the built-in lens IDs `anatomy` and `machines`. So a new pack's lens and kinds render with undesigned fallbacks, or a surface needs a change.
findings.evidence: design-language.md (Lenses: "one color per relationship kind"; the tokens `--block-service`, `--block-library`, `--block-store` and `--block-infra`); contracts.md:569 (LensDecl has id, label, relations, flow, level, default and empty text, with no color); architecture.md:1254 ("`Anatomy` is what the `anatomy` lens shows... `Machine` is what the `machines` lens shows").
findings.failure_scenario: In the S10 evidence run, the toy pack's `flags` lens on the canvas draws its edges in an arbitrary or default color that collides with another lens. The `flags.flag` blocks get no designed fill, which the screenshot critique against the design language flags.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `style = { yarn = "<palette slot>" }` to LensDecl and `block = "<slot>"` to KindDecl, chosen from a fixed palette in @planroom/ui. The palette's contrast test then covers every pack. Map views by result type (MachineView, Breakdown), not by lens ID.

verdicts.reason: The pack set really is resolved per process from the environment, while the store, active snapshots and folds are shared. No meta record of the pack set exists and no check spots a mismatch. The S10 ci_path sets PLANROOM_PACKS only on the scan line. The tool.check guard doesn't cover PLANROOM_PACKS, so an agent can load a policy-bearing pack. DR-48 holds back only `auto_enabled`: low-stakes prefills and `infer` outputs from such a pack still apply as inferred facts with no person involved. That breaks R10 consistency and R5, and can make the tier B scenario S10 fail as written. Nothing in the docs handles it.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:539 ("then `PLANROOM_PACKS` (colon-separated)... A person chose it by listing it in config or `PLANROOM_PACKS`, so loading it deals no card"); decisions.md:1157 (DR-60, same rationale); architecture.md:363 (active snapshot = last `scan` event); architecture.md:364 ("unknown kinds drop with a warning"); architecture.md:399-403 (the guard denies store files, person-only commands and `PLANROOM_PERSON_KEY`, but not PLANROOM_PACKS); architecture.md:818 (only `auto_at` is held back for out-of-tree packs; otherwise a result prefills by `stakes`); architecture.md:333-335 (prefill and infer outputs apply as inferred facts, not ghosts); feature_list.json:541-545 (PLANROOM_PACKS only on the scan step; `ask kinds`, `map --lens flags` and `decide` run without it). grep finds no packs_mismatch and no meta pack list: packs_hash appears only in the snapshots and blob_facts keys (architecture.md:461-463).

verdicts.reason: The contract really can't express several v0.1 kinds. `subject` is a node or edge kind, but `machines_same` (a machine pair) and `override_retarget` (an orphaned override) have neither as subject. Choice options are a static IndexMap, but `file_component` and `attach_target` choose among per-subject candidate nodes. The effect set is closed at five, and none of them retargets an override. Some `when` prechecks, such as "no path rule placed" and "within 10 lines of its anchor", are not field predicates. DR-17 says the engine never names a decision kind, so the natural workaround breaks the design's own R11 seam. It also leaves the S7 (tier A) eval and auto policy for `file_component` undefined. The closed effect set is part of the prompt-injection mitigation, so adding a retarget effect has to be designed, not improvised. Nothing in the docs supplies dynamic options or role subjects.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:615 (`subject: String // a node or edge kind`), :616 (`when` = field/value predicate), :630 (`Choice { options: IndexMap<String,String>, auto_choices }`), :620 (`effect` with five `do` values), :655 (EvalCase.label is "an option"); architecture.md:817 ("`effect` is a closed set of five kernel effects"); architecture.md:820 ("The kernel and engine never name a decision kind"); architecture.md:836, 840, 841, 842 (subjects: unplaced file, machine pair, orphaned override, next action with no target); architecture.md:788 (prechecks that are not field predicates); architecture.md:1308 (closed effects as an injection mitigation).

verdicts.reason: The gap is real. `drift`, `kinds`, `stage` and `lint` are listed as pack questions, but none of them is a pipeline of the twelve shapes, and machine pairing is assigned to no module. It doesn't make S6 or S10 fail, though. Machine drift already has a designed home in the one diff engine (`DiffKind::Machine`, served as `planroom ask drift`). The Jaccard pairing rule and thresholds are specified. `kinds` and `stage` are catalogue and plan reads that the composition root can serve. What's missing is the pack-data expressiveness of a few built-in questions and the placement of the pairing code, not a broken scenario or a KICKOFF constraint. The point about single-pack shapes is also weak: the two-pack bar governs new shapes, not the twelve recorded in DR-15. The part of this finding that affects decisions (the `machines_same` subject) is already covered by extensibility-2.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:996-1005 (`kernel::diff`, `DiffKind ... Machine`, and the row "Machine drift | the code machine | the doc machine | `planroom ask drift`"); architecture.md:735 (pairing rule: Jaccard 0.8 and 0.5, then `diff(machine A, machine B)` restricted to transitions); architecture.md:65 ("`drift` through the one diff engine"); architecture.md:722 and decisions.md:361 (the two-pack bar applies to a *new* shape); contracts.md:572-574 (closed Shape enum); architecture.md:728, 729, 733 (questions `kinds`, `stage`, `lint`, `drift`).

verdicts.reason: Real: an ID prefix belongs to one pack, and compose classifies services through the merged `[[image_roles]]`, which maps some images to `observability.infra`. So changing which pack classifies a service changes its ID. Not material, though. No tier A or B scenario changes the image-role set while overrides exist: S10's packs add no image roles, and its pack scan comes before any edits. When it does happen, nothing is lost silently. The fold raises `rescan.retarget`, which is bound to a person-stakes card whose default keeps the override detached and lists it in Diffs. That satisfies R6's "never silently overrides", and the edit is kept, so there is no data loss. In v0.1 the built-in pack set and its globs change only with an engine upgrade or an out-of-tree pack.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:304 (prefix shared within a pack only; "Two packs declaring one prefix is `pack_invalid`"); architecture.md:670 (observability pack maps collector, Prometheus and Grafana to `observability.infra`); architecture.md:367 ("A target that vanished raises the decision bound to the `rescan.retarget` role"); architecture.md:841 (`override_retarget`: person stakes, default "keep the override detached, listed in Diffs"); architecture.md:655 and feature_list.json:536-545 (the S10 flow has no overrides before the pack scan).

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real. The literal scan matches only built-in kind and relation names. The plan lint rules (MECE overlap, a Must below the MVP line, a ladder under 2 rungs) don't fit the four RuleTypes. So the kernel would have to hard-code plan prop names, which the scan can't see. Matching bare, generic kind names such as `file`, `state`, `step` or `job` can also make a new pack's kind collide with ordinary kernel literals. The docs handle only the machine prop names, which reach the kernel as shape parameters.
verdicts.evidence: repo-layout.md:132 (`domain_free`: no literal equals a built-in pack kind or relation name, with or without `<pack>.`); repo-layout.md:156 ("prop names reach machine checks as shape parameters": machines only); contracts.md:575 (RuleType `RequiresProp | RequiresEdge | MinChildren | Covers`); architecture.md:970-972 (MECE overlap, "a Must below the line", "a ladder under 2 rungs"); traceability.md:30 (`kernel/tests/lint.rs::mece_overlap`); architecture.md:728-733 (bare kind names such as `file`, `state`, `step`, `job`, `image`).

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real. `[[languages]]`, `[[image_roles]]` and the plan-only `[[stages]]` are special-purpose top-level tables. The docs say only that the first two "merge across loaded packs", with no precedence rule or duplicate-key rule for, say, two packs claiming `rb`. Two `default = true` lenses are likewise undefined. Tier has no Precise variant, although fact merging ranks precise first and SCIP is said to need "no kernel change". LinkerDecl is built-in only, so an out-of-tree pack's hint kinds have nothing to consume them. No document resolves these.

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real, by design. `requires` may be only `[]` or `["code"]`, and referenced kinds must belong to the pack, `code` or the kernel. So an out-of-tree pack can't extend observability, release, artifacts or machines without editing boundaries.toml and the loader. The self-test even treats `requires = ["observability"]` as a violation. That limits R11 for domains that build on any v0.1 domain other than code.
verdicts.evidence: repo-layout.md:142-143 (`requires = [[], ["code"]]   # the only allowed values`); repo-layout.md:158 ("every referenced kind belongs to the pack, `code` or the kernel"); repo-layout.md:173 (self-test step 6 expects `pack_invalid` for `requires = ["observability"]`); decisions.md:271 ("which in v0.1 means `code` or nothing").

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real. The templates use a bare `$file` (a path) as an edge's `from` and as a hint's `scope`, but the documented reference grammar lists only `@alias:`, an ID, `@id:KIND:KEY` and `@ext:`, and `from` is unspecified. Hint.scope is typed NodeId. A path is not a NodeId, so the runner must silently map paths to `code.file` IDs, which the docs never state. A `requires = []` pack would then rely on a code kind implicitly.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:564-569 (`from = "$file"`, `scope = "$file"`, and the reference forms for targets and parents only); architecture.md:643 and :649 (the Ruby pack uses `from = "$file"` and `scope = "$file"`); contracts.md:564 (the forms are documented on `to` only); contracts.md:371 (`pub scope: NodeId`).

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real. Plan item types are declared as `ItemType { id, props }` inside a plan-only `[[stages]]` table. That runs a second typing and prop-validation mechanism beside KindDecl, and no other pack can declare Intent-level item types. DR-45 chose `kernel.item` deliberately, but the docs don't explain why item types can't be ordinary kinds.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:577-580 (`StageDecl.items: Vec<ItemType>`, and `ItemType { id /* the kernel.item type */, props: Value }`); contracts.md:550-553 (KindDecl with `props`); contracts.md:545 and architecture.md:537 (`[[stages]]`, plan pack only); architecture.md:729 (plan items are `kernel.item` with a `type`).

verdicts.reason: Minor, and real. The design language assigns one yarn color per relationship kind and fixed block tokens named after code and observability kinds. LensDecl and RelationDecl have no color or style field, and KindDecl has only `icon`. The canvas opens Anatomy and Machine by the built-in lens IDs `anatomy` and `machines`. A new pack's lens therefore gets an undesigned color. Since `flags.flag` is a Code-level node, the block-fill point matters less, but the lens color gap stands.
